title: Inside SUMMARIZE, removing the filter on the group-by column does not widen the result: the cluster filters every column
query: "All Sales", CALCULATE ( SUM ( Sales[Amount] ), REMOVEFILTERS ( Product[Color] ) )

source.quote: Therefore, despite the removal of the filter from Product[Color] by REMOVEFILTERS , both Sales and All Sales calculations produce the same result.
source.supports: the article shows this query shape and says both columns are equal

source.quote: it creates a filter context using all the columns in the cluster, filtering the values that are present in the cluster
source.supports: the filter is on every column of the expanded Sales table, not just the colour

derivation: Sales rows by product colour (Bike and Helmet are Red, Lock is Blue, Scooter is Green): rows 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 are Red, rows 4, 6 are Blue, none is Green. Red cluster: 100 + 40 + 20 + 200 + 100 = 460; Blue cluster: 50 + 30 = 80. The cluster filter holds every column of the Sales rows in it (SalesKey included), so REMOVEFILTERS on Product[Color] leaves the same rows visible and All Sales equals Sales. The intuitive reading (540 in All Sales) is what the article warns against.
notes: This is why extension columns in SUMMARIZE are discouraged.
